# Croma Figma DS changes

## 0.5.1 — 11 November 2026

- Put editable component, token, asset, Storybook and test sources directly in Git.
- Add standard development commands, contributor guidance and pull request checks.
- Build and deploy Storybook from verified main-branch source with GitHub Pages.
- Add a repeatable release workflow that tags and packages the exact verified commit.
- Remove a Mac-specific package-check cache path.
- Support direct npm installation of versioned GitHub release packages.
- Component design and source-acceptance boundaries are unchanged from 0.5.0.

## 0.5.0 — 2026-11-05

- Added PlainSection, SurfaceCard and HelpDisclosure with shared grouping, card anatomy, accessible disclosure and one base plus one card surface in themed forms. Nested SurfaceCards flatten into plain subsections.
- PrototypeField owns 8px label and 12px hint/error spacing, forwards its input ref and uses one accent focus border. SearchCombobox uses one combined-control focus boundary and the same help spacing.
- SelectionPillGroup compact pills are text-only by default with hidden native input glyphs; icons and swatches are explicit. Card rows use equal responsive columns, invariant state geometry and immediate selection without fill transitions. Focus uses one contiguous inner stroke.
- Themed purchase/notification/search extensions share semantic surfaces and readable text. Light field error colour is reassigned from saved source paint278:81072 for contrast; original source components are unchanged.
- ActionGroup supports start/end/between alignment. SurfaceCard actions have shared spacing and align quiet-action labels with card copy. CompositionDialog uses page background and retains body scrolling/footer visibility.
- Added five Design hygiene compositions, component-specific authoring/migration guidance, and four regression cases. The extension suite is now part of figma:verify. Existing 0.4.0 adapter compatibility hooks remain.

Correction: No authored Figma component correction is made in this release.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-11-05

- Added SelectionPillGroup single/multiple selection with native input semantics and user-approved invariant geometry: green selected stroke/text, neutral grey selected fill and transparent unselected state with grey stroke.
- Added LiveCommerceHeader as a separate dated website-layout preset using logo/menu/search/location/account/cart anatomy; its original public account SVG is bundled. Original Figma Header and generic CommerceHeader remain separate.
- SearchCombobox exposes an inside-results heading/count contract; option semantics remain reserved for selectable suggestions.
- The annotation review distinguishes reusable DS extension gaps from adapter/consumer defects, including duplicate visual classes, double padding and local cascade/state rules. Application integration changes and business logic remain separate from library acceptance.

Frozen files remain unchanged in the separate version record.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-11-05

- Added SearchCombobox with controlled query, grouped model/storage/finish suggestions, optional brand filter, keyboard selection and loading/error/empty states.
- Added native-radio/checkbox SelectablePurchaseCard and Group, InlineNotification, LoadingIndicator and Breadcrumb compositions.
- Added fully editable CommerceHeader with original logo/icon slots and responsive navigation; the original raster-based Header reference remains separate.
- Added CompositionDialog, ResponsiveStepper, PrototypeField, InlineFieldAction, ActionGroup and PrototypeButton recipes for shared insets, body-only dialog scrolling, narrow layouts, long labels and stable loading actions.
- CTA authors use sentence case while preserving proper nouns/acronyms. CSS preserves supplied casing; no automatic lowercasing is applied.
- Geometry, theme-role assignments and composition spacing are explicitly extension choices. Routing, data fetching, business validation and exchange-prototype integration remain caller-owned.

Frozen files remain unchanged in the separate version record.

## 0.2.3 — 2026-11-04

- Stepper caller artwork is uniformly scaled and centred inside the written12pxicon slot; original SVG root geometry and asset bytes remain unchanged.
- Numbered Stepper acceptance examples no longer pass a placeholder plus icon.
- Added an Icon Steps review story covering both themes and both orientations with original source icons.

Frozen files remain unchanged in the separate version record.

## 0.2.2 — 2026-11-04

- User-approved reconsideration: retain the current source focus appearance as default and restore the previous outer outline as an optional alternate.
- FormField and Dropdown expose focusAppearance="source"|"outer-outline"; the alternate restores the earlier outer focus outline and Dropdown row rectangle. This is a presentation option, not a new authored Figma variant.
- Fields, floating labels, inputs, Dropdown text and review-story titles explicitly use normal upright font style; source typography sizes, weights, line heights and tracking remain unchanged.
- Added separate Previous focus outline alternate stories for Form Field and Dropdown.

CONTRIBUTING.md:
# Contributing to Croma DS

Use Node 22.12 or newer and npm. Clone the repository, run `npm ci`, then `npm run dev`.
Create a branch for a change and open a pull request against `main`.

## Component changes

1. Read the component's source evidence and the rules in `docs/FIGMA-DESIGN-HYGIENE.md`.
2. Update shared components in `packages/figma-ds/src` and shared tokens in `packages/figma-foundations`.
3. Add or update Storybook examples for the affected states, including dark surfaces and narrow widths.
4. Add a meaningful behavior regression when behavior changes. Keep original Figma components separate from prototype extensions.
5. Run `npm run verify`. Include the affected stories, source basis, changes and actual checks in the pull request.

Do not use prototype-specific CSS to disguise a missing shared rule. Do not change original artwork bytes or assert visual acceptance from a passing build. Never add the raw Figma archive, credentials, personal files or the private extraction corpus to this repository.

## Releases

Component changes and repository changes use semantic versions. A patch version can correct behavior or developer tooling without adding a component API. Update the root and all four workspace versions together, refresh `package-lock.json`, and update `CHANGELOG.md` and `RELEASE-NOTES.md` in the same pull request.

After the main branch passes checks, run **Actions → Publish release → Run workflow** with the matching version. The workflow rebuilds and tests, packages the exact commit, creates its version tag and publishes the packages, source, Storybook and checksums. Existing releases are never overwritten. The earlier 0.5.0 tag is the initial archive distribution checkpoint; 0.5.1 starts the source-backed developer repository releases.

Storybook deploys to GitHub Pages after checks pass on `main`. Pull requests run the same checks but do not replace the public Storybook. The existing shared 0.5.0 catalogue remains a frozen review reference until separately updated.

## Package registry

The release archives support ordinary `npm install` over HTTPS without signing in or downloading files manually. The package names resolve to `@croma/figma-ds` and `@croma/figma-foundations` inside the project.

These packages have not been published to npmjs.com. Publishing under `@croma` requires that scope's owner to grant access. Do not claim ownership of Croma's namespace or rename imports silently. An authorised npm account and confirmed namespace are needed before adding registry publishing. GitHub Packages also requires separate client authentication; it is not used for anonymous installation here.
README.md:
# Croma design system

Reusable React components and foundations built from Croma's actual Figma DS, with separately documented prototype extensions.

[![Checks and Storybook](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/actions/workflows/quality.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/actions/workflows/quality.yml)

[Storybook](https://hrithikbdc.github.io/Croma-Existing-DS/) · [Releases](https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Use in a prototype

Use React and React DOM 19. Install the two matching **0.5.1** packages directly; no ZIP download, GitHub login or npm registry login is required:

```sh
npm install --save-exact \
  https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases/download/v0.5.1/croma-figma-foundations-0.5.1.tgz \
  https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS/releases/download/v0.5.1/croma-figma-ds-0.5.1.tgz
```

Import the four stylesheets once at the application entry:

```tsx
import '@croma/figma-foundations/fonts.css';
import '@croma/figma-foundations/tokens.css';
import '@croma/figma-foundations/typography.css';
import '@croma/figma-ds/styles.css';
import {Button, PrototypeTheme} from '@croma/figma-ds';

export function App() {
  return (
    <PrototypeTheme Theme="dark">
      <Button Type="Filled">Continue</Button>
    </PrototypeTheme>
  );
}
```

Apply the page background to the entire document, including the app shell. The default dark page is `#191919`; the subdued card surface is `#212121`.

```css
html, body, #root { min-height: 100%; margin: 0; background: #191919; }
```

Use the documented shared components and tokens, remove conflicting legacy styles, and theme dialogs and overlays too. Read [design hygiene](docs/FIGMA-DESIGN-HYGIENE.md) and [prototype extensions](docs/FIGMA-PROTOTYPE-EXTENSIONS.md) before applying the DS to an existing prototype. Pin both dependencies to the same release and commit your lockfile.

The names `@croma/figma-ds` and `@croma/figma-foundations` are the installed import names. They are not currently published to npmjs.com. The HTTPS command above is the supported distribution route.

## Develop the library

Use Node **22.12+** and npm. The editable source is directly in the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/hrithikbdc/Croma-Existing-DS.git
cd Croma-Existing-DS
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Storybook opens at `http://localhost:6020`. Run `npm run figma:dev` for the consumer prototype at `http://localhost:5182`.

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Build the DS and start Storybook |
| `npm run build` | Build the components and consumer prototype |
| `npm run build:storybook` | Build the static catalogue |
| `npm run typecheck` | Check TypeScript after building the DS |
| `npm test` | Run consumer and component browser regressions against built apps |
| `npm run verify` | Build, typecheck, check source/package boundaries and run browser tests |
| `npm run release:pack` | Package a clean, already verified source commit |

Install Chromium before running browser tests: `npx playwright install chromium` (Linux CI uses `--with-deps`).

## Repository structure

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/figma-foundations` | Tokens, typography, Switzer and font notices |
| `packages/figma-ds/src` | React components, styles and source artwork |
| `packages/figma-ds/evidence` | Curated source values and acceptance records |
| `apps/figma-storybook` | Stories and documentation |
| `apps/figma-prototype` | Consumer examples and acceptance harness |
| `tests` | Behavior, composition and source checks |
| `docs` | Source limits and reusable design rules |
| `.github/workflows` | Checks, Storybook deployment and versioned releases |

## Review and release

Use a branch and pull request for component changes. Checks run on pull requests and main-branch changes. Successful main-branch checks deploy the current development catalogue to GitHub Pages. [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) describes the component and release process.

Release **0.5.1** starts source-backed developer releases. The earlier 0.5.0 tag records the initial archive distribution; its editable source is the named source ZIP in that release's assets. Existing downloads stay unchanged. The [shared 0.5.0 review catalogue](https://croma-figma-ds.bombaydc-3738.chatgpt.site) remains available separately.

Original Figma specifications take priority. Prototype extensions have separate implementation contracts. Full-system visual acceptance remains incomplete; builds and passing tests do not establish stakeholder sign-off.

No blanket open-source licence is asserted. Croma branding, artwork and supplied fonts retain their existing rights and notices. The raw Figma archive, private extraction corpus and credentials are excluded.
RELEASE-NOTES.md:
# Croma DS 0.5.1

11 November 2026. Developer distribution and repository improvements; component designs are unchanged from 0.5.0.

## Changes

The repository now contains editable foundations, React components, original artwork, Storybook stories, prototype examples and regression tests. Clone it and run `npm ci` then `npm run dev`. Main-branch changes build and test before Storybook deploys to GitHub Pages. Pull requests run checks without replacing the public catalogue.

The release workflow packages the exact verified commit and publishes both installable TGZs, editable source ZIP, static Storybook ZIP, changelog, release notes, manifest and SHA256 checksums. Existing releases are not overwritten. The package verification cache now uses the operating system temporary directory instead of a Mac-only path.

## Use in prototypes

Install both matching packages directly from the versioned release URLs using the command in README.md. React and React DOM 19 are peer requirements. Import all four DS stylesheets and use PrototypeTheme around the full page. No npm registry account is needed for the GitHub package URLs. Named npmjs.com distribution is not configured.

## Acceptance scope

The release workflow requires component builds, consumer builds, TypeScript, source-literal and package-boundary checks, Storybook build and the component/consumer browser suites to pass before publishing. Consult the successful workflow run for observed outcomes. A planned workflow is not evidence of a successful run.

Original Figma visual acceptance remains incomplete. These repository changes do not establish 100% visual acceptance or verify access from Croma's managed network. Older frozen releases and the existing 0.5.0 shared catalogue remain unchanged.
